source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 3: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
Yahan upar wale polynomial ki degree 3 hai aur neeche wale ki 2. Jab upar ki degree neeche ke barabar ya zyada ho to fraction improper kehlata hai.
Improper fraction par partial fractions seedha nahi lagte; pehle long division karni parti hai, bilkul jaise \(\frac{7}{2} = 3 + \frac{1}{2}\) likhte hain.
Division se ek polynomial (quotient) aur ek proper fraction (remainder wala) milega.
Plan: divide, remainder wale fraction ko Case-I se torna, phir har term ka alag integral.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 1}{x^2 - 1}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: yeh integral.
Tareeqa: numerator ki degree (3) denominator ki degree (2) se kam nahi, is liye pehle division. Partial fractions ka tareeqa sirf proper fraction (upar ki degree neeche se kam) par chalta hai; agar hum bina divide kiye \(\frac{A}{x - 1} + \frac{B}{x + 1}\) likh dein to equation kabhi poori nahi hogi.

Long division
\[(x^2 - 1)(x + 2) = x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 2\]
\[x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 1 = (x^2 - 1)(x + 2) + 1\]
Kyun: Pehle socha: \(x^2\) ko kis cheez se multiply karein ke \(x^3\) bane? \(x\) se. Phir \(2x^2\) ke liye \(+2\). Is tarah quotient \(x + 2\) aaya. \((x^2 - 1)(x + 2)\) ko numerator se minus kiya to sirf 1 bacha, yani remainder 1.

Integrand ko nayi shakal mein likhein
\[\dfrac{x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 1}{x^2 - 1} = x + 2 + \dfrac{1}{x^2 - 1}\]
Kyun: Dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder. Dono taraf \(x^2 - 1\) se divide kiya. Ab \(x + 2\) ka integral to bilkul aasaan hai, aur bacha hua \(\frac{1}{x^2 - 1}\) proper fraction hai.

Remainder wale fraction ke partial fractions
\[\dfrac{1}{(x - 1)(x + 1)} = \dfrac{A}{x - 1} + \dfrac{B}{x + 1}\]
\[1 = A(x + 1) + B(x - 1)\]
\[x = 1:\ A = \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[x = -1:\ B = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: \(x^2 - 1 = (x - 1)(x + 1)\) (difference of squares), yani do alag linear factors: Case-I. \(x = 1\) rakha to \(1 = 2A\); \(x = -1\) rakha to \(1 = -2B\).
Dhyan dein: \(B\) negative hai; minus sign yahan se aage tak saath chalega.

Har term ka integral
\[\int \left(x + 2\right)dx = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + 2x\]
\[\dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{dx}{x - 1} - \dfrac{1}{2}\int \dfrac{dx}{x + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}\ln|x - 1| - \dfrac{1}{2}\ln|x + 1|\]
Kyun: Polynomial wale hisse par power rule \(\int x^n\,dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}\); fractions par \(\int \frac{dx}{x + a} = \ln|x + a|\).

Sab ko jor dein
\[\int \dfrac{x^3 + 2x^2 - x - 1}{x^2 - 1}\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{x^2}{2} + 2x + \dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left|\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right| + c\]
Kyun: Log ka rule \(\ln|p| - \ln|q| = \ln\left|\frac{p}{q}\right|\) laga kar dono logs ko ek bana diya. Dono shakalein sahi hain; kitab ka jawab is doosri shakal mein hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\,\dfrac{1}{2}\ln\left|\dfrac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right| = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{x - 1} - \dfrac{1}{x + 1}\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{x^2 - 1}\]
Kyun: Bracket ke andar common denominator lene se \(\frac{(x + 1) - (x - 1)}{x^2 - 1} = \frac{2}{x^2 - 1}\) aata hai, aur \(\frac{1}{2}\) se multiply karke \(\frac{1}{x^2 - 1}\). Saath mein \(\frac{x^2}{2} + 2x\) ka derivative \(x + 2\) hai. Dono mila kar asal integrand wapas aa gaya.

blocks.text: Kitab ke aakhir mein answers (page 301) mein Exercise 3.4 ke jawab ghalat heading "Exercise 3.6" ke neeche chhape hain. Is sawal ka jawab us block ka item (iii) hai: \(\frac{x^2}{2} + 2x + \frac{1}{2}\ln\left|\frac{x - 1}{x + 1}\right| + c\). Yeh jawab sahi hai. Jis block par "Exercise 3.4" likha hai (page 301) woh kisi aur exercise ke jawab hain, is liye wahan se milane ki koshish na karein.
